name: testing
doc:
testing and the runtime half of `zell test`.

Test functions are marked @test: `@test func TestAdd(t *testing.T)` or
a plain `@test func Something()`; `@bench func BenchX(b *testing.B)`
(or `@test` with a *testing.B) is a benchmark (run with `zell test
--bench`). `zell test [path]` finds them, generates a driver calling
Main with every Case and runs it.

Isolation: Main runs every test in its own child process (the test
binary re-executes itself with --run-one), so t.Fatal, t.Skip and even
a panic end only that test. t.Run subtests run inside their parent's
process; a Fatal in a subtest ends the whole top-level test.

Parallel tests: a test whose body calls `t.Parallel()` (as a statement
of the test function; `zell test` finds the call when it discovers the
tests) runs concurrently with the other parallel tests, up to
`--parallel N` (default 4) child processes at a time, after the
sequential tests (each sequential test runs alone). Results are printed
in that order: sequential tests, then parallel ones by declaration.

testing.Panics(t, fn) checks that fn panics: fn runs on a thread of its
own whose panic is caught (no defers run in fn); where that is not
possible (Windows) the test binary re-runs the current test in a child
process up to that Panics call, where the child calls fn.

Assertions (testing.Equal(t, got, want) ...) report through t.Error and
keep going; the ...Fatal variants stop the test (testing.EqualFatal).

Fallible code: a test may return `void!` and use `?` (a returned error
fails it with `error: <message>` and the trace); `t.Must(f())` gives the
value of a `T!` call or ends the test with `file:line: <message>`, and
`t.MustFail(f())` gives its error or ends the test with `file:line:
expected an error`. Must and MustFail are compiler intrinsics (the only
calls taking an unhandled `T!`), not methods declared here.

Table tests are plain slices of structs:

  @test func TestAbs(t *testing.T) {
      var cases = [Case{In: -1, Want: 1}, Case{In: 2, Want: 2}]
      for c in cases {
          t.Run(fmt.Format("{0}", c.In), func(t *testing.T) {
              testing.Equal(t, math.IAbs(c.In), c.Want)
          })
      }
  }

items.name: PanicMessage
items.signature: func PanicMessage() string
items.doc:
The message of the last panic Panics caught on this thread ("" when it
ran the function in a child process).
items.summary: The message of the last panic Panics caught on this thread ("" when it ran the function in a child process).

items.name: Panics
items.signature: func Panics(t *T, fn func()) bool
items.doc:
Reports an error unless fn panics. fn runs on an OS thread of its own
inside a panic capture scope (runtime/ABI.md 8): a panic there ends that
thread only, without running defers or destructors of fn's frames (what
they own is leaked, locks they hold stay held), and Panics returns true;
the code of the test runs once. A panic on another thread (a task fn
started) still ends the test. Where the runtime cannot capture panics
(Windows), the test binary runs the current test again in a child
process (`--run-one` with a probe of this call) up to this call, where
the child calls fn and exits with the panic's status.
items.summary: Reports an error unless fn panics.

items.name: PanicsWith
items.signature: func PanicsWith(t *T, fn func(), want string) bool
items.doc: Like Panics, and the panic message must contain want.
items.summary: Like Panics, and the panic message must contain want.

items.name: True
items.signature: func True(t *T, cond bool, msg string) bool
items.doc: True reports an error with msg unless cond holds.
items.summary: True reports an error with msg unless cond holds.

items.doc: The handle of a running test.
items.summary: The handle of a running test.

members.name: Name
members.doc: Name returns the test name ("TestX/sub" for subtests).
members.summary: Name returns the test name ("TestX/sub" for subtests).

members.name: Failed
members.doc: Failed reports whether the test has failed.
members.summary: Failed reports whether the test has failed.

members.name: Skipped
members.doc: Skipped reports whether the test was skipped.
members.summary: Skipped reports whether the test was skipped.

members.name: Log
members.doc: Records a message (shown for failing tests and with -v).
members.summary: Records a message (shown for failing tests and with -v).

members.name: Error
members.doc: Marks the test failed and logs msg; the test continues.
members.summary: Marks the test failed and logs msg; the test continues.

members.name: Fail
members.doc: Marks the test failed (without a message).
members.summary: Marks the test failed (without a message).

members.name: Fatal
members.doc: Marks the test failed, logs msg and ends it.
members.summary: Marks the test failed, logs msg and ends it.

members.name: Must
members.doc:
Must returns the value of x, a call returning V! (the only argument
that may stay unhandled; x may contain await). If x fails, Must ends
the test as failed with the file:line of the call, the error message
and its trace. For a void! argument it yields nothing. A compiler
intrinsic (sema/testing.rs): only `t.Must(x)` is allowed.
members.summary: Must returns the value of x, a call returning V! (the only argument that may stay unhandled; x may contain await).

members.name: MustFail
members.doc:
MustFail returns the error of x, a call returning V! that is expected
to fail. If x succeeds, MustFail ends the test as failed with the
file:line of the call and "expected an error". A compiler intrinsic
(sema/testing.rs): only `t.MustFail(x)` is allowed.
members.summary: MustFail returns the error of x, a call returning V! that is expected to fail.

members.name: FailNow
members.doc: Ends the test now (failed if it was marked failed).
members.summary: Ends the test now (failed if it was marked failed).

members.name: Skip
members.doc: Skips the rest of the test.
members.summary: Skips the rest of the test.

members.name: Parallel
members.doc:
Marks the test as safe to run in parallel with the other parallel
tests. `zell test` finds the call statically (it must be a
statement of the test function); at run time it does nothing.
members.summary: Marks the test as safe to run in parallel with the other parallel tests.

members.name: Run
members.signature: func Run(name string, fn func(*T)) bool
members.doc: Runs fn as subtest name; returns true if it passed.
members.summary: Runs fn as subtest name; returns true if it passed.
